name: Congenital Myasthenic Syndrome with Kinetic Defect Due to Reduced Ion Channel Conductance
aliases: CMS with Ion Channel Conductance Defect

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Myasthenic Syndromes

criteria.description: Presence of fatigable muscle weakness with onset in infancy or early childhood
Electrophysiological evidence of neuromuscular transmission defect including decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes affecting ion channel conductance at the neuromuscular junction
Improvement of symptoms with acetylcholinesterase inhibitors or other neuromuscular junction targeted therapies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of fatigable muscle weakness with electrophysiological evidence of neuromuscular transmission defect and confirmation by genetic testing
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of clinical, electrophysiological, and genetic data.

searchTerms: muscle weakness that worsens with use

pathognomonic.symptomName: Decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation
searchTerms: muscle response decreases with repeated nerve stimulation
weakening muscle signals on nerve tests

common.symptomName: Dysphagia due to bulbar muscle involvement
searchTerms: difficulty swallowing due to throat muscle weakness
breathing difficulty from weak respiratory muscles
shortness of breath due to muscle weakness
mild eyelid droop that doesn't worsen with activity
slight loss of muscle bulk in arms or legs

rare.symptomName: Cardiac arrhythmias secondary to autonomic involvement
searchTerms: heart rhythm issues due to autonomic dysfunction
cardiac arrhythmias related to nerve involvement

imaging: Normal brain and spinal cord MRI
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes encoding neuromuscular junction ion channel subunits (e.g., CHRNE, CHRNA1)
other: Electrophysiological studies showing decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation

distinguishingFeatures: Autoimmune etiology with presence of autoantibodies
Later onset compared to congenital forms
Fluctuating weakness with response to immunosuppressive therapy
Facilitation of muscle strength with repeated stimulation
Autoantibodies against presynaptic voltage-gated calcium channels

redFlags: Bulbar muscle paralysis leading to aspiration risk
